description.en: Planets, paintings, penalties and paella: one quick lap around everything.
description.fr: Planètes, tableaux, penalties et paella : un petit tour de tout, en vitesse.
description.ar: كواكب ولوحات وركلات ترجيح وباييا: جولة سريعة حول كلّ شيء.
description.es: Planetas, cuadros, penaltis y paella: una vuelta rápida por todo.

questions.text: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explain: It is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.

questions.text: Which country has the largest land area?
questions.explain: It spans eleven time zones: somewhere in Russia, someone is always having breakfast.

questions.text: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explain: It was built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.text: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explain: Counting cold deserts too, the biggest of all is Antarctica.

questions.text: Counting overseas territories, which country has the most time zones?
questions.explain: Thanks to islands scattered across the oceans, France has 12.
questions.source: [VERIFY] French government / time-zone references (France: 12 zones incl. overseas, 13 with Adélie Land)

questions.text: On Venus, a day lasts longer than a year.
questions.explain: Venus spins so slowly that it goes round the Sun before it finishes one turn.
questions.source: [VERIFY] NASA 'Venus' (sidereal day ~243 Earth days; year ~225 Earth days)

questions.text: What is the smallest country in the world?
questions.explain: It covers less than half a square kilometre.

questions.text: Which country is shaped like a boot?
questions.explain: Sicily, just off the toe, looks like the ball it's about to kick.

questions.text: Which country has three capital cities?
questions.explain: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein share the job.
questions.source: [VERIFY] South African Government 'Capital cities' (Pretoria, Cape Town, Bloemfontein)

questions.text: What is the tallest waterfall in the world?
questions.explain: It drops about 979 m in Venezuela, so high the water turns to mist.

questions.text: Ants live on every continent except…
questions.explain: Australia, by contrast, is home to some of the most varied ants on Earth.

questions.text: Which gas do plants take from the air to make their food?
questions.explain: In return, they release the oxygen we breathe.

questions.text: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.explain: Insects have six, so spiders aren't insects: they're arachnids.

questions.text: What is the hardest natural material?
questions.explain: It tops the Mohs hardness scale at 10.

questions.text: Which planet has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot?
questions.explain: The storm is wider than the whole Earth.
questions.source: [VERIFY] NASA 'Jupiter: Great Red Spot' (storm wider than Earth)

questions.text: Which planet spins tipped on its side, rolling around the Sun?
questions.explain: Its axis is tilted by about 98 degrees.

questions.text: Bats are mammals.
questions.explain: They are the only mammals that can truly fly.
questions.source: [VERIFY] encyclopedia 'bat' (only mammals capable of true flight)

questions.text: What is the largest animal known to have ever lived?
questions.explain: Its heart alone is about the size of a small car.
questions.source: [VERIFY] NOAA Fisheries 'blue whale' (largest animal known to have lived)

questions.text: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explain: And its blood is blue. Ocean royalty.

questions.text: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explain: It was once used in most thermometers.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Royal Society of Chemistry periodic table 'Mercury'

questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explain: It comes from "aurum", the Latin word for gold.

questions.text: Which country produces the most coffee?
questions.explain: Ethiopia is where the coffee plant is thought to come from.

questions.text: Which part of the human body has no blood vessels and takes oxygen straight from the air?
questions.explain: That's why it stays perfectly clear.
questions.source: [VERIFY] ophthalmology refs (cornea is avascular; oxygen from air via tear film)

questions.text: Sound travels faster in water than in air.
questions.explain: About four times faster.
questions.source: [VERIFY] physics refs (speed of sound ~1,480 m/s in water vs ~343 m/s in air)

questions.text: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.explain: The Empire State Building is hit around 20 times a year.
questions.source: [VERIFY] NOAA / NWS lightning myths (Empire State Building struck ~20-25 times a year)

questions.text: Which animal has fingerprints so like ours that they could fool an expert?
questions.explain: Even under a microscope they are hard to tell apart.

questions.text: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explain: The next closest, Proxima Centauri, is over four light-years away.
questions.source: [VERIFY] NASA 'Sun' / 'Proxima Centauri' (nearest star beyond the Sun)

questions.text: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still stands today?
questions.explain: It's also the oldest of the seven.

questions.text: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explain: Leonardo was also an inventor who sketched flying machines.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Musée du Louvre 'Mona Lisa' (Leonardo da Vinci)

questions.text: In which city can you see the Mona Lisa?
questions.explain: She hangs behind protective glass at the Louvre.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Musée du Louvre (Mona Lisa location, protective glass)

questions.text: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explain: Buzz Aldrin followed him a few minutes later.

questions.text: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
questions.explain: It happened in July, with Apollo 11.

questions.text: Who developed the printing press with movable metal type in Europe?
questions.explain: He worked in Mainz, around the 1450s.

questions.text: Which Roman city was buried by Mount Vesuvius in AD 79?
questions.explain: The ash preserved streets, bakeries and even graffiti.

questions.text: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.explain: He proposed it in 1989 while working at CERN.
questions.source: [VERIFY] CERN 'The birth of the Web' (Tim Berners-Lee, 1989)

questions.text: The word "algebra" comes from a book by which scholar?
questions.explain: His own name gave us another word: "algorithm".

questions.text: The English word "coffee" traces back to which language?
questions.explain: It travelled from "qahwa" through Turkish "kahve" into Europe.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Online Etymology Dictionary 'coffee' (Arabic qahwa via Turkish kahve)

questions.text: Who painted "The Starry Night"?
questions.explain: He painted it in 1889, from memory of the view from his window.

questions.text: Painter Frida Kahlo came from which country?
questions.explain: Her Blue House in Mexico City is now a museum.

questions.text: Which artist is famous for painting melting clocks?
questions.explain: The painting is called "The Persistence of Memory" (1931).

questions.text: How many keys does a standard piano have?
questions.explain: 52 white and 36 black.

questions.text: Which great composer kept writing music after losing his hearing?
questions.explain: He wrote his Ninth Symphony when he was almost completely deaf.

questions.text: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.explain: A standard bass guitar usually has four.

questions.text: Tango was born on the Río de la Plata, in Argentina and which neighbour?
questions.explain: UNESCO lists tango as heritage shared by Argentina and Uruguay. Buenos Aires and Montevideo still argue about who danced first.

questions.text: Flamenco comes from which region of Spain?
questions.explain: It mixes song, guitar, dance and rhythmic hand-clapping called "palmas".

questions.text: Pop group BTS comes from which country?
questions.explain: Their 2020 hit "Dynamite" was their first song sung entirely in English.
questions.source: [VERIFY] trivial (BTS, South Korea); Billboard/Big Hit: "Dynamite" (Aug 2020), first all-English single

questions.text: In "The Lion King", what is the name of Simba's father?
questions.explain: The 1994 film is set in the African savanna.

questions.text: Who directed "Jurassic Park" (1993)?
questions.explain: He also directed "E.T." and "Jaws".

questions.text: "Bollywood" blends "Hollywood" with the old name of which city?
questions.explain: Bombay has been officially called Mumbai since 1995.

questions.text: What was Walt Disney's first feature-length animated film?
options: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.explain: It came out in 1937.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Walt Disney Archives 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs' (1937)

questions.text: Which was the first non-English-language film to win the Oscar for Best Picture?
questions.explain: The South Korean film won in 2020.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Academy Awards database, 92nd ceremony (Parasite, Best Picture)

questions.text: How many players does each football team have on the pitch?
questions.explain: One of them is the goalkeeper, the only one allowed to use their hands.
questions.source: [VERIFY] IFAB Laws of the Game, Law 3

questions.text: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups?
questions.explain: Brazil has five titles.

questions.text: Which country hosted the very first FIFA World Cup, in 1930?
questions.explain: Uruguay also won it.
questions.source: [VERIFY] FIFA '1930 FIFA World Cup Uruguay' (host and winner)

questions.text: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar?
questions.explain: The final against France ended in a penalty shoot-out.
questions.source: [VERIFY] FIFA 'Qatar 2022 final' (Argentina beat France on penalties)

questions.text: At the 2022 World Cup, which team became the first from Africa to reach the semi-finals?
questions.explain: It was also a first for an Arab team.
questions.source: [VERIFY] FIFA Qatar 2022 (Morocco: first African and Arab semi-finalist)

questions.text: How often are the Summer Olympic Games normally held?
questions.explain: Tokyo 2020 was a rare exception: it took place in 2021.
questions.source: [VERIFY] IOC (Summer Games every 4 years; Tokyo 2020 held in 2021)

questions.text: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.explain: They stand for the union of the continents.

questions.text: In tennis, what is a score of zero called?
questions.explain: Then a game goes 15, 30, 40… and nobody fully agrees why.

questions.text: Roughly how long is a marathon?
questions.explain: Exactly 42.195 km.

questions.text: Pizza Margherita comes from which Italian city?
questions.explain: Tomato, mozzarella and basil: the colours of the Italian flag.

questions.text: Guacamole is mainly made from…
questions.explain: It comes from Mexico, where the avocado was first grown.

questions.text: Saffron, the priciest spice by weight, comes from which part of a flower?
questions.explain: Each crocus flower gives just three threads, picked by hand.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'saffron' (stigmas of Crocus sativus; priciest spice by weight)

questions.text: Paella comes from which Spanish region?
questions.explain: It's traditionally cooked outdoors in a wide, shallow pan.

questions.text: Which nut is used to make marzipan?
questions.explain: Ground almonds and sugar, shaped into fruits, animals and more.

questions.text: Botanically speaking, the tomato is a fruit.
questions.explain: Botanists even class it as a berry.

questions.text: The Great Wall of China can be seen from the Moon with the naked eye.
questions.explain: Even from low orbit it is very hard to spot with the naked eye.
questions.source: [VERIFY] NASA Earth Observatory 'Great Wall from space' myth

questions.text: Goldfish have a memory of only three seconds.
questions.explain: Experiments show they can remember things for months.
questions.source: [VERIFY] animal-cognition studies on goldfish memory (months, not seconds)

questions.text: Which language has the most native speakers?
questions.explain: English wins if you count everyone who speaks it as a second language.

questions.text: Which alphabet is Russian written in?
questions.explain: It's named after Cyril, a 9th-century scholar from Thessaloniki.

questions.text: How do you say "thank you" in Japanese?
questions.explain: "Konnichiwa" is hello, "sayōnara" goodbye, and "kawaii" cute.

questions.text: Which planet has the shortest day?
questions.explain: It spins once in about ten hours, despite being the biggest planet.

questions.text: Which letter appears in none of the 50 US state names?
questions.explain: Z is in Arizona, X in Texas and J in New Jersey.
questions.source: [VERIFY] list of US state names (no letter Q)

questions.text: Which bird can fly backwards?
questions.explain: Its wings can beat dozens of times a second.

questions.text: In which country would you find Machu Picchu?
questions.explain: The Inca citadel sits high in the Andes, about 2,400 m up.
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO WHC 'Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu' (Peru)
